maria: Heads up — seeing ~30% token latency regression on model xg-3-small after PR #872. Baseline tests (seq_len=2048, batch=1) are slower. I captured traces: nsys + torch.profiler (nv timeline). Uploaded artifacts to gs://redwood-profiling/maria/1813456789/ (trace.nsys, torchprof.json, run.log). Can someone from eng-runtime help triage? Steps to repro in container:
```
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
python -m torch.distributed.launch --nproc_per_node=1 run_server.py --model xg-3-small --seq 2048
nsys profile --output=trace --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=clock python run_infer.py --batch 1 --seq 2048
```
Thanks!

kevin: @maria grabbing artifacts now. Quick Q: did you pin cudnn / cuda versions? CUDNN autotuner or library changes can shift kernel selection. Also was kv-cache warm? Cold-start often inflates numbers. :eyes:

maria: cudnn 8.2.1, cuda 11.7, kv-cache was cold for this capture. I can rerun a warm-cache capture if that helps.

sam: +1 to warm run. Also can you share the exact torch.profiler config? Flamegraphs are super helpful to map CPU->CUDA stacks. If you used record_function marks that makes it easier.

maria: torch.profiler config is in the bucket (torchprof.json). Snippet I used:
```
with torch.profiler.profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], record_shapes=True, profile_memory=True, with_stack=True) as prof:
    model(input)

prof.export_chrome_trace('torchprof.json')
```

danielle: I'll generate a flamegraph from the nsys output. Minimal flow I use: export collapsed stacks from Nsight and then run flamegraph.pl. Example:
```
nsys-ui trace.qdrep -> export collapsed stacks (callstacks)
./stackcollapse.pl callstacks > collapsed.txt
./flamegraph.pl collapsed.txt > flame.svg
```
Ping me if you want the SVG dropped into the same bucket.

profiling-bot: artifact processed — quick summary: CUDA kernel time increased ~28% at step 12, memcpy HtoD spike (~3x) around 1.2s, and more frequent kernel launches observed. Summary: https://artifacts.redwood/prof/1813456789/summary

kevin: I'll try to repro locally tonight with the same docker image. If anyone can run a warm-run (kv-cache primed) with identical env and post the new traces under the same path with suffix "-warm", that would speed debugging. @sam can you also glance at build flags (ATen/CUDA) — suspect cudnn fallback or a new kernel path.

maria: adding warm-run to my queue now, will post new traces under gs://redwood-profiling/maria/1813456789-warm/ when done. Thanks for the quick responses :thumbsup:
